title: Chinese companies aren't winning overseas just because they're cheaper, Goldman Sachs says
summary:
Chinese companies aren't winning overseas just because they're cheaper, according to Goldman Sachs, challenging one of the biggest assumptions behind China's export boom.
More than a race to the bottomGoldman analyzed 11 sectors and 40 Chinese and global companies to study where Chinese firms are gaining market share.
Chinese products typically enter new markets at about a 30% discount to incumbent rivals, but prices often rise in subsequent years.
"These price cuts typically are initiated by companies who have been losing market share and trying to defend their market share in a very challenging situation and competition," Chen said.
Chen said Chinese companies tend to gain market share fastest in modular, consumer-facing, high-growth products.

title: G20 finance ministers, central bankers gather amid fallout from Iran war
summary:
The G20 finance ministers and central bank governors are gathering in Bangkok, Thailand, on Thursday amid an uncertain global outlook shaped by the US-Israel war on Iran.
Here are some of the key details about the meetings:What are the G20, the IMF and the World Bank?
Together, the G20 countries account for about 85 percent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and three-quarters of global trade.
The World Bank, also based in Washington, DC, primarily serves as a provider of loans and grants to developing countries.
Most finance ministers and central bank governors of the G20 will be in Bangkok, along with IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and World Bank Group President Ajay Banga.

title: Starlink restrictions affecting Ukraine's front line operations, Kyiv says
summary:
New restrictions on the speed at which some of Ukraine's weapons can travel and stay connected to the Starlink internet network have disrupted Ukraine's battlefield "missions", President Volodymyr Zelensky's adviser has warned.
Serhiy Beskrestnov said Ukraine had not been told about speed limits set overnight at 100mph (160km/h) by Elon Musk's SpaceX company.
Starlink is a vital tool allowing Kyiv to effectively guide drones to Russian targets and also protect Ukrainian skies.
It comes as at least 600,000 people across Ukraine were left without electricity after deadly overnight Russian missile and drone strikes, Zelensky said.
Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

title: US lifts sanctions on Venezuela’s top legislator
summary:
Jorge Rodriguez has been removed from OFAC’s sanctions list in latest US push for oil control and bilateral diplomacy.
The United States Department of the Treasury has lifted sanctions on the head of Venezuela’s National Assembly, Jorge Rodriguez, brother of the country’s interim President, Delcy Rodriguez.
The top lawmaker in the country, Jorge Rodriguez has held the position of National Assembly president since 2021.
He served as vice president under Venezuela’s late President Hugo Chavez, among other posts.
As interim president, Delcy Rodriguez has promised to hold elections – including in her recent remarks at the United Nations General Assembly – but no firm date has been set.

title: US charges 14 over North Korean IT worker scheme at more than 70 companies
summary:
The US Justice Department has charged 14 people over a North Korean job scam, announced on Tuesday.
North Korean IT workers used stolen names to get remote jobs at more than 70 US firms.
The workers earned about $3 million, which went to North Korean groups under US sanctions, prosecutors believe.
From 2019 to around July 2025, the workers used fake or stolen ID papers to apply, the indictment says.
North Korean hackers have also built their own AI tools for attacks, and hidden malware in fake software packages aimed at coders.

title: X suspends 13,000 accounts, alleging foreign influence ahead of US midterms
summary:
The social platform says networks targeted US political conversation across the spectrum ahead of midterm elections.
The social media platform X has suspended more than 13,000 accounts related to three suspected foreign influence operations linked to Iran, Russia and China that sought to shape the political debate in the United States.
X said its investigations found the networks used fake accounts to post and amplify political content targeting candidates and public figures “across the political spectrum”.
AdvertisementX has previously acted against suspected foreign influence networks.
In 2021, Twitter, as X was then known, said it had suspended 238 accounts purportedly operating from Iran.
